name: Close
tagline: Track deals and manually log communication in a focused sales workspace

tiers.name: Solo
tiers.limits: Exactly 1 user, up to 10,000 leads, 250 custom fields, 500 AI credits/month; no workflows

tiers.name: Essentials
tiers.limits: Unlimited leads/contacts, 250 custom fields; pooled 1,000 AI credits/user/month capped at 10,000/month; no workflows

tiers.name: Growth
tiers.limits: Unlimited leads/contacts, 250 custom fields, 250 custom activities and 50,000 custom-activity instances/month; pooled 1,500 AI credits/user capped at 15,000/month

tiers.name: Scale
tiers.limits: Unlimited leads/contacts and call-recording retention; 250 custom fields, 250 custom activities, 50,000 custom-activity instances/month; pooled 2,000 AI credits/user capped at 20,000/month

tiers.name: Custom
tiers.limits: Custom pricing and limits for larger or more complex sales teams

pricing.freeTierCaps: no free tier (14-day trial; no credit card required)
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (discount varies by tier, up to 50%)
pricing.hiddenCosts: Included AI credits refresh monthly and do not roll over; extra AI credits are sold separately. Calling, SMS and email usage can generate separate usage charges, and lower tiers omit workflows.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Close, track deals and manually log communication in a focused sales workspace. The hard boundary is built-in email, calling, sms, power dialer, workflows, and sales reliability, plus integrations, data quality, and workflow lock-in.
coreLoopDIY: Manage contacts and companies in a focused sales workspace, move deals through a pipeline, manually log communication, and surface the next action.
whatYouLose: built-in email, calling, SMS, power dialer, workflows, and sales reliability
moatNotes: integrations, data quality, and workflow lock-in
ongoingBurden: deduplication, permissions, imports, sync, enrichment, email capture, automations, backups, and audit history
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Close because CRM value compounds as the system becomes the shared memory of every customer interaction and embeds itself in the rest of the stack. The recurring cost buys deduplication, permissions, imports, sync, enrichment, email capture, automations, backups, and audit history, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Twenty
priorArt.desc: Active open-source modern CRM with extensible data models.

alternatives.name: EspoCRM
alternatives.desc: A traditional CRM that actually lets you change the data model; polished enough, but still your server.

facts.dataFormat: CRM records in MySQL, MariaDB or PostgreSQL; uploaded files on the application server
facts.gapVsPaid: It does not match Close's tightly integrated calling, SMS and sales-sequence workflow, so communications are more fragmented.
facts.setupBlocker: A server with PHP and a supported database, or Docker; production also needs HTTPS, mail, backups and upgrades

alternatives.name: Frappe CRM
alternatives.desc: A clean leads-and-deals board with notes, tasks and email; Frappe underneath means a real server, not a toy.

facts.install: Frappe Cloud signup, or easy-install script, Bench or Docker
facts.dataFormat: CRM records in the Frappe site database; attachments in the site's file storage
facts.gapVsPaid: Its calls, messaging and outbound sequences are not as unified or mature as Close's communication-first workspace.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting means Linux plus Frappe Bench or Docker, database and Redis services, a domain, mail configuration and upgrades

alternatives.name: HubSpot Free CRM
alternatives.desc: A real two-seat CRM for free; 1,000 contacts is where the upsell starts counting.

facts.dataFormat: Records and files live in HubSpot's cloud; CRM records can be exported as CSV or XLSX
facts.gapVsPaid: The free product does not provide Close-level native calling, SMS and outbound sequencing in one focused sales screen.

alternatives.name: Twenty
alternatives.desc: A modern pipeline CRM with custom objects, views and mailbox sync; the subscription becomes a Compose file.

facts.dataFormat: CRM data in PostgreSQL, jobs and cache in Redis, and files in local or object storage
facts.gapVsPaid: It lacks Close's deeply integrated calling, SMS and sales-sequence experience.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting needs Docker Compose, environment variables, a domain, email, persistent storage, backups and upgrades

alternatives.name: Odoo CRM One App Free
alternatives.desc: A full hosted pipeline for unlimited users, provided CRM is the only Odoo app you marry.

facts.dataFormat: CRM data and attachments live in Odoo Online's managed database and filestore
facts.gapVsPaid: It lacks Close's communication-first calling, SMS and sequence workflow, and the one-app rule punishes expansion into other Odoo modules.
facts.setupBlocker: None for CRM alone; installing a second Odoo app ends the one-app-free arrangement

alternatives.name: Zoho CRM Free
alternatives.desc: A full little CRM for three users and 5,000 records; the wider Zoho maze is optional.

facts.dataFormat: Records and attachments live in Zoho's cloud; record imports and exports use CSV
facts.gapVsPaid: The free tier does not reproduce Close's native calling, SMS and sales-sequence depth.

alternatives.name: Freshsales Free
alternatives.desc: A clean three-user pipeline with email and mobile apps; useful automation starts asking for rent.

facts.dataFormat: CRM records and files live in Freshworks' cloud; contacts and deals can be imported or exported by CSV
facts.gapVsPaid: The free tier lacks the advanced calling, sequencing and automation that make Close a communication-first CRM.

alternatives.name: Bitrix24 Free
alternatives.desc: Contacts and deals for a small team, wrapped in enough menus to qualify as indoor architecture.

facts.dataFormat: CRM records, chats and files live in Bitrix24's vendor cloud and Drive storage
facts.gapVsPaid: Its sprawling suite and crowded interface are substantially less focused than Close's compact sales communication workspace.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Startup plan and a personal or very small-team CRM DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Close in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and Docker Compose; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: manage contacts and companies in a focused sales workspace, move deals through a pipeline, manually log communication, and surface the next action.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create contacts, companies, opportunities, notes, tasks, and configurable pipeline stages.
Add fast global search, duplicate detection, merge, CSV import, and CSV export.
Provide a chronological interaction timeline with manual email and meeting logging.
Implement saved views, filters, owner assignment, and a next-action dashboard.
Add role-based access, an immutable activity log, backups, and a recovery command.
Seed a realistic demo workspace and document field mapping for imports.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out automatic mailbox ingestion.
Deliberately leave out commercial enrichment databases.
Deliberately leave out enterprise forecasting, integrations, and compliance.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
